interest: U.S. legal analysis of territorial waters around the former Japanese mandated islands.
keywords: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.0145/1-247) consists of January 1947 legal memoranda generated by the Office of the Legal Adviser regarding the breadth of territorial waters surrounding the former Japanese mandated islands in the Pacific (the Marshall, Caroline, and Mariana Islands). Prepared by Leonard C. Meeker and John Howard for inclusion in the Department of State's documentation book supporting the proposed United States strategic trusteeship agreement, the primary five-page legal analysis examines whether island groups under unitary administration possess territorial waters encompassing all enclosed waters or only a fixed three-mile belt around each individual island. Concluding that established international law and firm U.S. policy restrict territorial sovereignty to a three-mile marginal sea per island despite vast inter-island expanses, the file also includes transmittal memoranda from Meeker to James F. Green in the Division of Dependent Area Affairs and Legal Adviser Charles Fahy submitting the study for final clearance.

subfiles.about: Legal memorandum analyzing the extent of territorial waters surrounding the former Japanese mandated islands and concluding that sovereignty is limited to a three-mile belt around each island.
subfiles.from: Leonard C. Meeker and John Howard
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive legal memorandum analyzes whether the territorial waters of former Japanese mandated island groups (the Marshalls, Carolines, and Marianas) cover all waters enclosed by the groups or only a fixed three-mile band around individual islands. The authors conclude that international law and traditional United States maritime policy limit territorial waters to a three-mile belt around each separate island, while recognizing limited jurisdictional rights on the adjacent high seas for protective purposes such as hovering laws and neutrality defense. The analysis reviews historical doctrines including the cannon-shot rule, the 1930 Hague Codification Conference's deliberations on archipelagos, an 1877 British Order in Council, and King Kamehameha III's 1854 neutrality proclamation in Hawaii. It determines that proposed geometric solutions to eliminate high-seas pockets within archipelagos have minimal practical application to Micronesia due to the vast distances separating the islands.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Territorial Waters of Former Japanese Mandated Islands
